function: Learns a binary per-user and per-target CSI updating policy (re-estimate or predict from temporal correlation) in each frame; beamforming then solved by non-learned FP/SCA (pp. 6-8).
system: MISO ISAC with full-duplex OFDM BS (64 transmit, 32 receive antennas), 6 single-antenna users, 3 radar targets; 5.89 GHz, 10 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Deep reinforcement online learning: fully connected DNN actor with order-preserving quantization, critic solves FP/SCA beamforming per candidate, DNN retrained online from replay memory with cross-entropy loss (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom simulation: frequency-flat temporally correlated communication CSI (Jakes-based correlation, empirical path loss), radar target-state model; DNN learns online over 10,000 simulated frames; no dataset (pp. 3-4, 10-11).
test_conditions: Online training and evaluation on the same simulated stream (10,000 frames), fixed 6 users and 3 targets; Fig. 9 repeats with other weights, user distances, target states (pp. 11, 14).
baselines: Non-learned only: exhaustive-search genie, random update (probability 0.5), all update, each with FP/SCA or MRT beamforming; no earlier learned method compared (pp. 11-12).
metrics: System utility, relative utility ratio to exhaustive search, weighted communication rate, weighted radar tracking error and cost, CSI re-estimation frequency and counts (Figs. 5-9, pp. 11-14).
complexity: Qualitative only: polynomial complexity versus exponential 2^(K+Q) for exhaustive search; Fig. 8 shows explored candidate decisions per frame; no FLOPs, parameters, or runtime (pp. 10, 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "the temporally correlated communication CSI model is given by". Custom frequency-flat temporally correlated model with empirical path loss (p. 10); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "To further assess algorithm robustness, we consider different distances for each user". The DNN learns online on one simulated stream and Fig. 9 repeats it with other settings; no model trained in one condition is reported tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "we perform an exhaustive search of all potential CSI updating decisions". All baselines are non-learned (exhaustive search, random update, all update, MRT); no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall DROL method is an efficient algorithm only requiring polynomial complexity". Qualitative; no order expression, FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime is given, and Fig. 8 (p. 13) only counts explored candidate decisions.
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider that the system is operated on the carrier frequency of 5.89 GHz". The setting is simulated with no dataset, and no code or data link or DOI appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Borderline function: the DNN learns only the CSI re-estimate-or-predict decision (CSI acquisition timing in ISAC), while estimation (LMMSE, EKF) and beamforming (FP/SCA) are non-learned. Included as area 2 (channel estimation in an ISAC system) because pilot and echo re-estimation timing is a physical-layer function; reviewer to confirm it is not above_phy scheduling, and that area 5 (ISAC resources) is not the better fit. q4 is 0 because 'polynomial complexity' is qualitative and Fig. 8 counts explored decisions only; reviewer to confirm.
